getoutofhere.text: GetOutOfHere sprays wide and wins anyway: among the very best tracked in the matchups, fast on the trigger, and standing firm when the opposition stiffens. The aim wanders, the accuracy sits near the bottom, yet the shots that land tend to land in the head. A young account, so the story is early, but the first pages are loud.

ghastl.text: ghastl is a storm of a player: matchup rating and activity both among the very best, with a relentless pace and an accuracy near the top. The edge softens a touch when the opposition gets hardest, the one wrinkle in an otherwise elite card. Lifetime numbers and matchups agree, with the lifetime IvI sitting among the very best too.

gx20.text: gx20 fights like a storm that never runs out of rain: near the top of everyone tracked, fierce no matter who shows up. Nothing rattles them against the hardest opposition. The accuracy and headshots both sit near the top, and the lifetime numbers back up the matchups. The sample behind this one is older and smaller, so take it as a sketch, not a portrait.

genialtester.text: Since 2013, GenialTester has played an efficient game: in the elite bracket, with a matchup kill-death figure near the summit. The aim sits mid-pack on the lifetime board, which makes the matchup numbers the more interesting half of the story. The lifetime ledger runs a touch cooler than the matchups, which keeps the tale honest.

glassheavn.text: Glassheavn has no weak spot, just a strong game all the way through: at the top of the matchups, unbothered by harder foes, and the edge holding strong against the strongest third. Bravery is the headline here: the harder the enemy, the stronger the showing. Lifetime numbers agree with the matchups, which makes this one a clean, complete card.

gladboystr.text: GladBoysTR brings a complete game: top shelf nearly everywhere, steady as the opposition strengthens, and sharp with every shot. The headshot rate sits near the top, and the lifetime ledger tracks the matchups closely. Treat this one as a sketch: the opponent sample behind it is older and smaller.

generallawson.text: GeneralLawson wins fights the matchup board rates among the very best, yet the aim itself sits below average and the lifetime board lands squarely mid-pack. The resistance is near the top, the bravery holds above average, and the toe-to-toe kill-death tally stays elite — results built on judgment rather than precision. A fighter whose choices, not whose crosshair, do the hard work.

gladboys.text: GladBoys thrives as the opposition gets tougher: bravery near the very top, resistance right there alongside, and a matchup mark that keeps climbing. Pace runs hot, the aim stays precise, and a strong headshot share rides along with the volume. The lifetime board rates them even higher than the matchups do, and the consistency holds up, so the whole card reads like a fighter built for the hardest rooms.

ghostonly.text: GhostOnly is a young account making a spectacular entrance: every line near the top, with headshots at the very best tracked and a lifetime board to match. Pace is relentless and the game rises with the opposition. The one wrinkle is the edge against the strongest third, which dips below average — an early read, but the first pages already carry weight.

guerrillatactics.text: GuerrillaTactics strikes fast and keeps striking: a matchup rating in the top shelf, kill pace near the very top, and bravery that holds as the opposition improves. Headshots run above average, so the volume comes with a sharp edge. The consistency mark lands mid-pack, the one dip on an otherwise strong card.

gladboysvs.text: GladBoysVS hits the field like a storm front: every adjusted line sits in the upper tier, from rating and tempo to bravery and resistance, the matchup kill-death mark keeping the same ground. The aim is razor-clean — accuracy and headshot share both top-shelf — with the lifetime numbers landing right alongside the matchups. Consistency is the one merely middling line on an otherwise relentless card.

grr0g.text: GRR0G has been winning fights since 2015: the rating stands near the top, the work rate sits near the top, and bravery and resistance back it up. The aim stays sharp and headshots land near the top, with lifetime numbers near the top as well. The matchup kill-death mark lags the rest a touch, the single modest line on the card.

gzzzt.text: Gzzzt is a study in selectivity: bravery near the very bottom, yet resistance and the close-quarters kill-death record sit among the very best tracked. The tempo is deliberate, below average on both kill measures, and headshots are rare — the kills come from body shots placed with care. The lifetime IvI sits near the bottom, far below the matchups, which is exactly what a patient, picky game produces.

gentlereleaseonyourface.text: GentleReleaseOnYourFace brings a storm of pressure: activity, bravery, and resistance all near the top, with output near the very top. Accuracy sits near the top and the headshot share well above average. The lifetime IvI sits near the top too, closing a card that rarely gives the opposition room to breathe.

gtgd.text: GTGD has been at this since 2012, and it shows: resistance and matchup kill-death near the top, with bravery and activity well above average. Accuracy sits near the top, while the headshot share lands mid-pack. The lifetime numbers sit well above average, backing a long, steady record of winning the fights that matter.

grrog.text: Grrog has been at it since 2013, and the game still sings: output near the very top, a game that climbs with the opposition, and resistance to spare. The aim is sharp, headshots land often, and the lifetime numbers back the matchups up. Only against the strongest third does the edge soften — a veteran with hardly a wrinkle.

grrrrraaaaawwwwvvvvvyyyyyyyyyyyy.text: GRRRRRAAAAAWWWWVVVVVYYYYYYYYYYYY roars onto the card: pace at the very top, a game that sharpens as the opposition improves, and accuracy to match. Headshots land often, the lifetime numbers sit among the best, and the resistance holds steady. The edge softens a touch against the strongest third — a loud game with a quiet flaw.

geilo20.text: Since 2013, geilo20 has been a fixture at the sharp end: matchup rating, tempo, bravery, resistance — all of them upper tier, and the matchup K/D figure ranks near the very best. Brisk pace, steady aim, and a lifetime board that matches the matchups. A veteran who has kept the standard high for over a decade.

ghostspartan25rt.text: GhostSpartan25RT is the matchup board's best argument for itself: among the upper tier of the matchup board, with a guard that holds against fast finishers and a one-on-one kill-death count near the top. The headshot share sits near the very bottom, the lifetime IvI right beside it — yet the matchups hold near the top. The one caveat: versus the strongest third, the edge falls away fast.

gingerbabynce.text: GingerBabyNCE wins duels the hard way: top-tier in the matchups, sprightly in tempo, and bravery that rises with the opposition. The aim wanders badly — accuracy and headshots both sit near the bottom — yet the head-to-head kill-death line lands well above average. The lifetime board is far humbler than the duels, which makes this one a puzzle worth a second look. A player whose duels belie the raw aim.

generalye.text: GeneralYe plays with authority: a top-shelf rating, a relentless tempo, and a lifetime kill-death line among the very best. The matchups agree the ranking is earned, and the edge narrows a touch when the pressure peaks. A veteran who sets the pace and keeps it.

gammelan.text: GaMmeLaN plays the long game and wins it: upper tier by the matchup numbers, a tempo to match, and bravery that holds under heavier fire. The lifetime board sits a notch below the matchups. The IvI line sits close behind. Against the toughest opposition, the results stay respectable — a veteran who is ready for every fight.

godmode.text: GodMode has been winning matchups since 2013: a top-tier rating, resistance near the top, and bravery that holds as the opposition gets tougher. The lifetime kill-death line sits near the top while the matchup kill-death figure lands above average, a neat split. The edge holds up against the toughest third too, which rounds out a strong, steady card.

g500player.text: G500PLAYER is a veteran of the long game, fighting since 2014: in the upper tier of the matchup rankings, measured on the trigger, and steady under fire. The edge softens a little against the toughest lineups, the one blemish on an otherwise strong card. The lifetime numbers and the matchups point the same way, which keeps the story simple.

gf0ce.text: gf0ce plays a game with no loose threads: a matchup rating sitting in the top bracket, a brisk tempo, and resistance that stands up to stronger opposition. The headshot share sits mid-pack, the one ordinary line in a strong card. The toughest third barely dents the edge; it stays steady rather than sharp. A reliable presence who keeps turning up and keeps winning their share.
